data_objects.name: mass_spectra
data_objects.meaning: A tab-separated collection of mass-spectrum records. Each row couples a variable-length peak list to molecular-structure, formula, mass, precursor, and adduct metadata.

variables.name: identifier
variables.meaning: Spectrum-record identifier in the form MassSpecGymID followed by digits; it is the candidate row key, although uniqueness was not checked exhaustively and the numeric suffixes are not contiguous in file order.

variables.name: mzs
variables.meaning: Comma-separated mass-to-charge values for the spectrum's peaks. The list is positionally aligned with intensities and was ascending in every sampled row.

variables.name: intensities
variables.meaning: Comma-separated peak-intensity values positionally aligned with mzs. Every sampled spectrum had a maximum value of 1.0, consistent with per-spectrum relative scaling, but the normalization convention is not declared.

variables.name: smiles
variables.meaning: SMILES representation of the molecular structure associated with the spectrum; sampled strings may encode stereochemistry.

variables.name: inchikey
variables.meaning: Short molecular key labeled as an InChIKey. Sampled values are 14-character strings and repeat across spectra having the same molecular metadata.

variables.name: formula
variables.meaning: Molecular formula associated with the represented parent molecule and SMILES string.

variables.name: precursor_formula
variables.meaning: Formula assigned to the precursor ion; sampled differences from formula are consistent with the row's proton or sodium adduct notation.

variables.name: parent_mass
variables.meaning: Numeric mass associated with the parent molecule before the precursor adduct is represented. The public file does not state the mass convention or unit.

variables.name: precursor_mz
variables.meaning: Mass-to-charge value assigned to the precursor ion represented by precursor_formula and adduct.

variables.name: adduct
variables.meaning: Ion/adduct notation for the precursor. Bounded samples contained protonated [M+H]+ and sodium-adducted [M+Na]+ values; this is not an exhaustive category inventory.

structure.description: The TSV has one header row and 231,104 data rows. The observation unit is one spectrum record, with identifier serving as the apparent spectrum-level key; row order has no declared semantic meaning.

Within a row, mzs and intensities are variable-length comma-separated arrays whose elements align one-to-one by position. In 800 rows sampled from eight blocks across the file, the arrays always had equal lengths, m/z values were ascending, and no field was empty.

Molecular and precursor metadata can repeat across several identifiers while the peak arrays differ, giving a repeated-spectrum, many-rows-to-one-represented-molecule pattern. No separate molecule table or acquisition-metadata object is present in the public root.

uncertainties: The file provides no embedded data dictionary or acquisition metadata, so instrument type, ionization source, collision energy, MS level, experimental provenance, and the reason for repeated spectra cannot be established.
The exact meaning and unit of parent_mass, including whether it is monoisotopic or another mass convention, are not declared.
The observed maximum intensity of 1.0 suggests normalization, but the denominator, preprocessing, and interpretation of intensity values are not documented.
The 14-character inchikey values resemble only part of a standard full InChIKey, but the file does not define how they were produced or which molecular distinctions they retain.
Identifier uniqueness, complete missing-value behavior, complete adduct vocabulary, and peak-array invariants were assessed only through bounded sampling rather than exhaustive value profiling.
annotation_notes: Evidence was limited to the mandated dataset-semantics skill and the public artifact massspecgym.tsv; no task, description, private, gold, grader, output, or existing-annotation artifacts were inspected.
Physical inventory: one 257,027,435-byte ASCII TSV with ten columns and very long lines.
Representative inspection covered the header, beginning and ending records, eight spread-out individual records, and 800 rows in eight bounded blocks.
